scenes.text: This $1.25 delivery text wants more than $1.25

scenes.head: The text
scenes.label: SAMPLE · MADE UP
lines: USPS: Your package is on hold. Pay the $1.25 redelivery fee within 24 hours: usps-redeliver-help.top
scenes.note: Fake number, fake link. Don't type it.

scenes.head: The tells
scenes.label: SPOT THEM
lines: 1. A tiny fee: the real target is your card number
2. "usps" inside a different web address
3. A 24-hour deadline

scenes.head: What to do
scenes.bad: Tap the link and pay the fee
scenes.good: Type usps.com yourself and track it there
scenes.note: Then forward the text to 7726 and delete it.

end.tagline: Source: US Postal Inspection Service, smishing

scenes.text: "Hi Grandma, this is my new number"

scenes.head: The text
scenes.label: SAMPLE · MADE UP
lines: I dropped my phone, this is my new number. I need $400 for a bus home. Please don't tell Mom.

scenes.head: The tells
scenes.label: SPOT THEM
lines: 1. New number + money, in one message
2. "Don't tell Mom" stops the one call that ends it
3. No name: it works on anyone

scenes.head: What to do
scenes.good: Call them on the number you already have
scenes.note: A family code word settles it in seconds.

end.lead: Send this to the family group chat

scenes.text: Got an "unpaid toll" text? Read this first

scenes.head: The text
scenes.label: SAMPLE · MADE UP
lines: FINAL NOTICE: unpaid toll balance of $6.99. Pay now to avoid a $50 late fee and license suspension.

scenes.head: The tells
scenes.label: SPOT THEM
lines: 1. License threats over a few dollars
2. A web address that isn't your toll agency
3. People get it who never used a toll road

scenes.head: What to do
scenes.good: Log in to your toll account the usual way
scenes.note: Or call the number on the agency's own website.

end.tagline: Source: FTC consumer alert, unpaid toll texts

scenes.text: The "fraud alert" that is the fraud

scenes.head: The text
scenes.label: SAMPLE · MADE UP
lines: Did you try an $892 purchase? Reply YES or NO. A specialist will call to verify you with the code we just sent.

scenes.head: The trick
scenes.label: HOW IT WORKS
lines: They try to sign in as you
Your bank texts you a real code
The "specialist" asks you to read it back

scenes.head: What to do
scenes.bad: Read the code to the caller
scenes.good: Hang up, call the number on your card
scenes.note: Your bank won't ask you to read a code back.

end.lead: Send this to someone who banks on their phone

scenes.text: A pop-up says call Microsoft. Don't.

scenes.head: The pop-up
scenes.label: SAMPLE · MADE UP
lines: Your computer is infected with 3 viruses. Do NOT close this window. Call Microsoft Support now.

scenes.head: The tells
scenes.label: SPOT THEM
lines: 1. Real Microsoft and Apple warnings never ask you to call
2. "Do NOT close" keeps you stuck
3. The goal: remote access to your computer

scenes.head: What to do
scenes.note: Won't close? Ctrl + Shift + Esc opens Task Manager on Windows.
